THE SCORING TRAP ON THAT ISSUE, STATED PLAINLY SO YOU DO NOT WALK INTO IT. Its title has two halves ('have failures reached production' AND 'how do institutions respond'), and cycle 12 genuinely advanced both: existence is now multi-source and multi-institution, and the response half produced a real finding (EY withdrew and issued an AI-responsibility statement; ENISA retained both reports, silently patched links, said 'human errors', and as of 2026-07-29 still carries no AI disclosure on either page). BUT ITS BASE-RATE QUESTION IS UNANSWERED AND IS BLOCKED BY SCOPE, NOT BY EVIDENCE VOLUME -- cycle 10 recorded exactly this when it capped the issue, and cycle 12 confirmed it deliberately rather than papering over it. Two named incidents are two data points, not a rate. src-0011 is NOT the CTI base rate and its own candidate_resolution is marked 'proposed' with the reason written into the summary: different population (peer-reviewed conference papers, which have reviewers; CTI reports have none), a ghost-citation definition keyed to absence from academic databases that is largely inapplicable to CTI footnotes (news/vendor URLs), and a per-PAPER denominator that is not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492. A score that treats a second anecdote plus an adjacent-population audit as a resolved base rate would be the single most likely error of this cycle. Read state/knowledge/src-0011.md's Limitations section before scoring, not after.
